definitions.explanation: describes behavior or words that are clearly pretended or insincere

examples.japanese: {白々|しらじら}しい{嘘|うそ}をつくな。
examples.english: Don't tell such an obvious lie.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{言|い}い{訳|わけ}は{白々|しらじら}しかった。
{知|し}っているくせに{白々|しらじら}しい{顔|かお}をしている。
examples.english: Even though they know, they're pretending not to with a straight face.

notes:
USAGE:
- {白々|しらじら}しい{嘘|うそ} (blatant lie)
- {白々|しらじら}しい{態度|たいど} (feigned attitude)
- {白々|しらじら}しい{顔|かお}をする (to put on an innocent face)

NUANCE:
Strongly implies the speaker can see through the pretense. Used when someone's deception or insincerity is painfully obvious.

RELATED:
- {空々|そらぞら}しい (similar meaning - forced, unnatural)
- {白|しら}を{切|き}る (to feign ignorance)

FORMS:
- Adverb: {白々|しらじら}しく
